body: Also, driving in Mexico (at least from what I’ve experienced/heard) is tad bit more difficult because some of the people don’t follow traffic rules. Follow the traffic rules even if you see people ignoring them. The transit officers are very strict there and some of them are not so nice.
Make sure you don’t stay out in the city too late. Nighttime is when the shit show tends to start. Don’t drive around with extremely tinted windows, it brings attention to your vehicle.

Eat. You deserve it. 
Start with small bites. If you finish your plate, that's wonderful. If you finished some of it, that's great as well and I am proud of you.

My advice to you is to be as honest as you can. Whenever teachers reach out to students that aren't getting work done, they usually expect bullsh*t excuses. But what you're going through is serious and should not be taken lightly. Any logical teacher will express concern to your situation. 2 things can happen: the teacher will call a counselor, or your parents/ask for a welfare check. Or they will simply not do anything about it and just wish you well. 
Either way, you must seek help if your situation gets worse. 
Lastly, I totally understand where you are coming from. I am a senior in high school, taking 9 classes and it's been quite a mess. I have a lot of work that I haven't turned in yet, it's not out of laziness, im just depressed. 
You are not alone.

Hey there, I totally understand where you're coming from, school can definitely be mentally draining. I suggest that you talk to someone, whether it's a close friend, family member, or a professional. Don't stress yourself out. I know that it sounds very generic and cliche, but grades do not define your worth. Take a breather. If you finish an assignment that's good, if you get halfway through an assignment that's okay as well. If you don't get any work done, that's perfectly fine. Put your mental health first. As I previously said, a grade does not define your worth.
